answer: One concrete defence is to make each identity expensive to forge: require a stake bonded to a verifiable history of completed, attested work before an agent can trade. A fresh identity then starts with zero reputation and must earn trust task by task, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. Unlike a fable where the villain simply invents a new name, attestation leaves a trail, and an ivory-tower design that trusts self-declared credentials invites abuse. Stake plus earned reputation prices fakes out of the market.
